subject: Post-demo: integration gating checklist for deployment mode decision
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Long <sarah.long@medsys.io>, Michael Chen <michael.chen@medsys.io>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Post-demo: integration gating checklist for deployment mode decision

Hi Sarah / Michael —

Thanks again for taking the demo call earlier. Quick recap and the specific items we need from your side to decide between Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, or Private (VPC / on-prem):

Key integration constraints we captured:
- Identity: SSO type (SAML 2.0 vs OIDC), IdP metadata, SCIM provisioning needs, role mappings.
- Keys & encryption: Do you require BYOK (customer-controlled keys)? HSM-backed keys? KMS provider (AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault / GCP CMEK)?
- Logging & retention: How long do logs need to be retained? Do you need raw request payloads accessible for audits? Audit log forwarding (SIEM syslog/S3)?
- Network & residency: VPC peering, egress restrictions, or on-prem requirement for any workload.
- Compliance artifacts: SOC2 / penetration test evidence and any attestation timelines for procurement.

Action items for MedSys (please reply inline):
1) Confirm IdP type and whether you can provide SAML metadata (or OIDC discovery URL).
2) Confirm KMS model: Redwood-managed keys acceptable, or do you require BYOK with HSM? If BYOK, which provider/model?
3) Logging retention requirement (months/years) and whether logs must be stored in your cloud account.
4) Expected peak QPS and average token size for inference (helps sizing Dedicated).

Attachments: integration-questions.xlsx (simple form you can fill), redwood-deploy-options.pdf (high-level mode comparison).

Suggested next steps: if you can answer 1–3 above, we can produce a short matrix mapping those answers to the recommended deployment (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) and follow with a technical deep-dive. I have tentative availability tomorrow 10:00 PT for a 30-minute follow-up — happy to lock that if it works.

Thanks —
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0142
From: Sarah Long <sarah.long@medsys.io>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Chen <michael.chen@medsys.io>, MedSys DevOps <devops@medsys.io>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 17:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo: integration gating checklist for deployment mode decision

Thanks Alex — great walkthrough. Quick answers/notes from our side and a couple of follow-ups: 

- Identity: We use Okta (SAML 2.0). Can provide metadata and SCIM is available but we'd prefer to scope provisioning later. Role mapping: yes, we'll provide a draft mapping.
- Keys: Procurement will ask for BYOK. Our preferred path is AWS KMS with import into a CloudHSM-protected key. Is Redwood able to accept a CloudHSM-backed key or do you need a different flow?
- Logs: Compliance requires 7 years for audit logs; we don't need raw PII request payloads stored for that long but audit-level logs (request ID, timestamps, model used, requester) must be retained and exportable to our S3.
- Sizing: Initial pilot ~50 QPS peak, average prompt+completion ~800 tokens. We expect growth after pilot.

Procurement note: we'll need SOC 2 Type II and pen test summary to start contracting conversations — timeline goal: decision by end of June.

Confirming the 10:00 PT tomorrow works for us. I'll attach a short internal security note after I check with CloudOps.

—Sarah
Sarah Long
Director, Cloud Ops | MedSys Health
sarah.long@medsys.io
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Long <sarah.long@medsys.io>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 08:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo: integration gating checklist for deployment mode decision

Sarah — perfect, thanks for the clear answers. A few clarifications and an initial mapping based on what you said: 

- Okta (SAML) — good, we'll take the metadata and draft role map. SCIM can be deferred to a later iteration.
- BYOK + CloudHSM: short answer — Full BYOK with CloudHSM backing is supported on our Private deployment (customer-managed KMS + HSM). For Dedicated capacity we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS (CMEK) but with more limited HSM integration (we can encrypt model caches and logs with your KMS key; direct HSM appliance attestation is only in Private/on-prem). Hosted uses Redwood-managed keys only. I will have Rishi add precise constraints below.
- Logs: 7-year retention is fine — we can export audit-level logs to your S3 and lifecycle them per your policy. Raw request payload retention for that long is unusual; we recommend keeping request payloads for 90 days unless you have a specific audit requirement.
- Sizing: 50 QPS / 800 tokens -> suggest Dedicated for pilot if you want predictable latency and control; Private if BYOK-HSM + strict network residency are non-negotiable. Hosted could work for initial proof-of-concept if you accept Redwood-managed keys and shorter retention.

Attaching sso-kms-compatibility-matrix.csv (matrix mapping typical IdP/KMS/HSM combos to deployment mode).

Next steps:
- Rishi to confirm exact HSM/attestation options and provide any additional security caveats.
- MedSys to share Okta metadata and preferred KMS key ARN (or confirmation that you will import a key into CloudHSM).
- I will prepare a short one-page recommendation and accompanying SOW options for Dedicated vs Private based on your answers.

See you at 10:00 PT.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Long <sarah.long@medsys.io>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 10:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo: integration gating checklist for deployment mode decision

Hi Sarah / team — quick technical note from Security/Infra: 

- CloudHSM-backed BYOK: Private (VPC / on-prem) supports a model where the customer controls the KMS/HSM and we perform an attestation flow. For AWS CloudHSM you would import keys and provide the KMS key ARN; we support wrapping keys with your HSM in Private. We will need details on the HSM model and whether you require FIPS 140-2 Level 3 attestation.
- Dedicated: we can integrate with customer-owned AWS KMS (CMEK). That provides key separation and control, but Dedicated runs in our managed environment and does not provide the same physical key custody guarantees as Private. If procurement insists on HSM appliance-level custody, Private is required.
- Logs: we can stream audit logs to your S3 via secure transfer (server-side encryption with your KMS key). For any retention >365 days we recommend lifecycle policies on your bucket — our export will not incur retention limits on our side.
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II report and pen test summary are available; I'll share the redacted artifacts in the shared Drive link. We can also produce an architecture whitepaper for the Private PKI/HSM flow.

Recommended technical next step: technical deep-dive between our infra engineers and MedSys CloudOps (45–60 minutes). We'll come prepared with a short checklist to validate HSM model, network peering, and key attestation steps. If you confirm the Okta metadata and a KMS ARN beforehand we can tailor the session.

Attachment: hsm-integration-notes.txt

—Rishi Malhotra
Head of Security & Platform Compliance | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
